extraction.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
extraction.description: The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) spans 8 embedding tasks covering a total of 58 datasets and 112 languages. It aims to provide clarity on how models perform on a variety of embedding tasks and serves as the gateway to finding universal text embeddings applicable to a variety of tasks.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB consists of 58 datasets covering 112 languages from 8 embedding tasks: Bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, STS and summarization.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Datasets are sourced from various public APIs and repositories, including arXiv, bioRxiv/medRxiv, Reddit, StackExchange, and others like BEIR, SemEval, and Tatoeba.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For clustering tasks, S2S datasets use only titles, while P2P datasets concatenate title and abstract. Some datasets are framed in both S2S and P2P settings.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MTEB imposes no limit on input length, leaving it up to models to truncate if necessary. Datasets are grouped into sentence to sentence (S2S), paragraph to paragraph (P2P), and sentence to paragraph (S2P) categories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations include labels for classification, clustering categories, similarity scores for STS, relevance for retrieval, and human assessments for summarization. Annotations are created by humans or derived from existing benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB is versioned at dataset and software level for reproducibility. JSON files corresponding to all results are made available. The benchmark is open-source and welcomes contributions via pull requests.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MTEB aims to make selecting the right embedding model easier and simplify future embedding research, potentially impacting industry applications and research progress.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark has limitations such as task imbalance (e.g., summarization has only one dataset), lack of very long documents, and limited multilinguality in retrieval and clustering tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: 1) No very long document datasets, 2) Task imbalance with some tasks underrepresented, 3) Multilinguality limited in retrieval and clustering, 4) No code datasets, 5) No additional modalities like images.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Dataset use cases include Training, Testing, and Validation for embedding models across tasks like classification, clustering, retrieval, STS, etc. Usage guidelines are provided through the benchmark's API and leaderboard.
